overview: Endeavour Mining is the largest gold producer in West Africa and a senior global gold miner, operating five producing mines - Sabodala-Massawa (Senegal), Ity and Lafigué (Côte d'Ivoire), and Houndé and Mana (Burkina Faso) - plus the Assafou development project in Côte d'Ivoire targeted for a final investment decision by year-end 2026. The company is LSE primary-listed (also TSX: EDV, OTCQX: EDVMF), reports in USD under IFRS, and produced 1,209koz of gold in FY2025 at an AISC of $1,433/oz. Its strategy centres on maintaining a high-quality, large/low-cost/long-life mine portfolio, organic growth via exploration and project development, and returning cash to shareholders.

business_model.summary: Endeavour is a single-commodity gold producer that generates nearly all revenue from selling gold doré bars (refined into London Good Delivery bars) at prevailing spot/market gold prices, with minimal hedging since completing its growth phase. Cash flow is highly leveraged to the gold price and to per-mine cost performance (AISC); there is no recurring subscription-type revenue - output is sold continuously as produced, so revenue is transactional/volume-and-price driven rather than contracted. The company also earns small by-product (silver) credits. Customers are global bullion buyers/refiners rather than retail; value is also shared extensively with host governments via taxes, royalties and dividends on minority government stakes (10-20% free carries in each mine).
business_model.customer_type: Gold doré sold to LBMA-approved refiners/bullion buyers; effectively a commodity price-taker with full exposure to spot gold since completion of hedge book roll-off in 2025
business_model.geographic_mix: Production split roughly Côte d'Ivoire ~35%, Burkina Faso ~34-39%, Senegal ~34% of FY2025/FY2026E group production (geographic mix trending more diversified as Lafigué/Sabodala-Massawa grow and Assafou is added in Côte d'Ivoire)

competitive_position.market_position: Largest gold producer in West Africa and ranked among the world's top 10-15 senior gold producers by output (~1.2Moz/year), with a portfolio skewed toward low-cost, long-life assets; the company explicitly screens its asset base against target criteria (+10-year mine life, >250koz/year, industry-leading AISC).

moat_factors.factor: Regional scale and in-house project delivery
moat_factors.description: Five mine builds completed in the last decade, each on time, on budget and in under two years, using an in-house projects team - a demonstrated execution advantage over peers who use external EPC contractors and face greater cost/schedule overruns.

FY2025 AISC of $1,433/oz was near the top of the peer group's cost curve historically but has risen with royalty inflation at higher gold prices; FY2026 guidance of $1,600-1,800/oz remains competitive versus a ~$1,457-1,500/oz industry average, though the gap to peers has narrowed as royalties bite across the sector.

95% national workforce, 86% in-country procurement, and status as one of the largest private-sector taxpayers in Senegal/Côte d'Ivoire/Burkina Faso support a strong social licence, but this is also a source of risk given reliance on continued government goodwill amid rising resource nationalism in the Sahel.

20.7Moz of Measured & Indicated resources discovered since 2016 at a sector-leading <$25/oz discovery cost; new 2026-2030 target of 12-15Moz at <$40/oz gives visibility on replacing depletion and extending mine lives beyond the 10-year target.

Net debt/EBITDA of just 0.07x at FY2025 year-end (vs 0.5x target ceiling) and $1.2bn of available liquidity give Endeavour unusual flexibility to fund Assafou construction and maintain shareholder returns without re-leveraging, a differentiator versus more leveraged peers.

weaknesses: Concentrated in three countries (Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso) all located in the geopolitically volatile Sahel/West Africa region, with Burkina Faso under military government and a track record of mine nationalisation in neighbouring Mali and within Burkina Faso itself (Boungou/Wahgnion)
AISC margin and cost position have eroded versus history as royalty rates scale with the elevated gold price, partially offsetting the benefit of higher realised prices
No meaningful commodity diversification - 100% gold price exposure with largely unhedged production since 2025
Mana and some legacy assets have shorter remaining mine lives/declining production, requiring continuous reserve replacement to sustain the portfolio
Single large growth project (Assafou) concentration risk - delays, cost overruns, or permitting issues would materially affect the long-term growth narrative to 1.5Moz by 2030

growth_drivers: Assafou development project in Côte d'Ivoire - DFS confirms 320koz/year production (first 8 years) at AISC of $1,026/oz, 16+ year mine life, $5.1bn after-tax NPV and 55% IRR at $4,000/oz gold; FID targeted by year-end 2026 with first gold expected H2-2028
Sabodala-Massawa underground expansion (Golouma/Kerekounda deposits) targeting +350koz/year supplementing CIL production from FY2027, with first underground ore expected late H2-2026
Group production growth target of +1.5Moz annual production by 2030 (vs. 1,209koz in FY2025), a ~27% increase from continuing operations

2026-2030 exploration strategy targeting 12-15Moz of new Measured & Indicated mineral resource discoveries (6-9Moz brownfield, 6Moz greenfield) at a sub-$40/oz discovery cost, using AI-enabled target generation across ~80 identified targets

Selective new-ventures exploration beyond West Africa in under-explored but prospective jurisdictions (e.g., Kazakhstan joint venture with East Star Resources) meeting strict +3Moz/1.5g/t/10-year mine-life criteria
Active portfolio management - continued divestment of non-core/depleting assets and reinvestment in large, low-cost, long-life assets to sustain class-leading cost position

Record high gold prices (reaching over $4,500/oz in 2025 and above $4,000/oz through mid-2026) providing substantial operating leverage and funding capacity for growth capex and shareholder returns simultaneously

business.description: Revenue, margins and valuation are entirely tied to the gold price; AISC guidance is itself calibrated to a $3,000/oz assumption, and a sustained price correction from current elevated levels (~$4,000-4,500/oz) would compress margins and free cash flow materially.

business.risk: Reserve/resource depletion and mine life risk
business.description: Group reserves of 16.6Moz (2025) require continuous exploration success and conversion to sustain the >10-year production visibility target; failure to replace depletion at several maturing assets (e.g., Mana) would erode the long-term production profile.

Despite a strong 5-for-5 on-time/on-budget construction track record, Assafou is a larger, more complex cornerstone project; delays to FID, permitting, or construction (24-30 month build) would push back the 1.5Moz by 2030 target.

A contractor fatality occurred at the Mana mine in February 2024; TRIFR increased to 0.99 in 2025 (above the 0.70 internal target), reflecting ongoing operational/safety risk inherent to large-scale underground and open-pit mining.

financial.risk: Royalty and cost inflation at high gold prices
financial.description: Royalty rates in Endeavour's host countries scale with the gold price, so AISC guidance of $1,600-1,800/oz for FY2026 (up from $1,433/oz actual in FY2025) partly reflects higher royalty burden eating into the benefit of higher realised prices.

Revenue is 100% USD-denominated but ~69-70% of operating costs are in CFA franc (euro-pegged) and euro; a weaker USD (as seen in 2025, Dollar Index down ~12%) raises dollar-translated costs, only partly offset by favourable cash translation.

Assafou's $1,061m upfront capital requirement, alongside Sabodala-Massawa underground expansion capex, will materially increase growth capex from 2026 onward, even though balance sheet capacity (0.07x leverage, $1.2bn liquidity) currently provides ample headroom.

regulatory.risk: Resource nationalism / nationalisation risk in the Sahel
regulatory.description: Burkina Faso's military government nationalised Endeavour's divested Boungou and Wahgnion mines (sold to Lilium Gold) for roughly $80m versus the originally agreed $300m sale value, following an arbitration settlement reached in August 2024; Mali has separately nationalised the Yatela, Morila and SOMIFI gold assets and revised mining conventions since its 2024 Mining Code changes. While Endeavour's remaining Burkina Faso assets (Houndé, Mana) continue to operate and the company reports constructive government dialogue, the regional trend materially raises headline political/expropriation risk for any Sahel-exposed miner.

regulatory.risk: Evolving mining codes and fiscal terms
regulatory.description: Côte d'Ivoire and Burkina Faso have both made regulatory changes aimed at increasing government/local-supplier economic shares (new Mining Code discussions in Côte d'Ivoire); rising royalty rates and potential further fiscal term changes could continue to compress realised margins even as gold prices stay high.

Growth projects (Assafou, Sabodala-Massawa underground) and exploration targets depend on timely environmental and exploitation permit approvals and licence renewals from host governments; delays or non-renewal would directly affect the growth pipeline.

macro.description: The investment case, shareholder returns programme (contingent on gold price staying at or above $3,000/oz) and project economics are all highly sensitive to a pullback from the current historically elevated gold price environment driven by central bank buying, a weaker USD and geopolitical uncertainty.

Military governments, coup risk, and shifting regional alliances (ECOWAS exits by Mali/Burkina Faso/Niger) create an unstable operating backdrop; while Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal are viewed as relatively more stable, Burkina Faso in particular carries elevated security and political risk.

Gold prices and the CFA franc/euro-pegged cost base are both sensitive to US Federal Reserve policy and dollar strength; renewed dollar strength or faster-than-expected rate normalisation could both pressure gold prices and the macro backdrop supporting investment demand.

Trade and supply chain disruption risk from regional insecurity (armed groups in border areas of Burkina Faso/Mali) could affect logistics, input costs and workforce safety, though Endeavour mitigates via long-dated, delivered-to-site supplier contracts and in-country sourcing (86% of procurement).

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold prices reached record highs above $4,500/oz in 2025 and remained elevated through mid-2026 (~$4,000-4,600/oz), driven by central bank buying, a weaker US dollar, elevated geopolitical risk, and continued safe-haven/ETF demand; the World Gold Council and most analysts expect continued but more moderate price support into 2026-2027, with risk skewed to a correction if real rates rise or the dollar strengthens sharply.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Gold mining is a commodity-cyclical business with revenue and margins directly tied to the spot gold price; Endeavour's largely unhedged production profile since 2025 means full exposure to both upside and downside price cycles, though operating costs (AISC) and royalty burdens also flex with the price, providing a partial natural offset.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high indirect sensitivity: lower real interest rates (and dollar weakness) have historically supported gold prices and thus Endeavour's revenue and cash flow; the company carries very low financial leverage (0.07x net debt/EBITDA), so direct balance-sheet interest rate sensitivity is low.
key_input_costs: Diesel/fuel and power (partially mitigated via solar/grid investments)

recent_developments.event: Record FY2025 results: 1,209koz gold production at $1,433/oz AISC, adjusted EBITDA of $2.3bn (55% margin), free cash flow of $1.2bn, net debt/EBITDA reduced to 0.07x, and record shareholder returns of $435m ($350m dividends + $85m buybacks); share price rose 171% in 2025, the third-best performer on the FTSE 100.

Environmental and exploitation permits for the Assafou project approved; Definitive Feasibility Study published 23 April 2026 confirming 320koz/year production (first 8 years), AISC of $1,026/oz, 16+ year mine life, $1,061m upfront capital, $5.1bn after-tax NPV and 55% IRR at $4,000/oz gold.

H1-2026 production of 564koz at AISC of $1,871/oz (within FY2026 guidance range); record H1 free cash flow of $761m (+19% YoY); net cash position of $254m; H1 shareholder returns of $301m ($230m dividends + $71m buybacks, +39% YoY); reiterated FY2026 guidance of 1,090-1,265koz production at $1,600-1,800/oz AISC; raised FY2026 sustaining capital guidance from $230m to $280m.

Sabodala-Massawa underground expansion progressing - dewatering of Golouma pit complete, underground mining contractor and fleet mobilising, with first underground ore targeted late H2-2026 and commercial underground production expected 2027-2028.

Board changes: Alison Henwood appointed Independent Non-Executive Director (effective 13 January 2026); Livia Mahler (Remuneration Committee Chair) to step down at the 2026 AGM after nine years; Morgan Carroll (former Chief Commercial Officer, with Endeavour since 2011) departed.

Endeavour reached an arbitration settlement with the Burkina Faso government and Lilium Gold resolving the divestment of the Boungou and Wahgnion mines, which were subsequently nationalised into the state-owned miner SOPAMIB for a fraction of their originally agreed ~$300m sale value - illustrative of the resource nationalism trend affecting Sahel-based gold miners, though it does not affect Endeavour's current five-mine operating portfolio.

Broad sell-side Buy/Outperform consensus as of August 2026 (BofA, Barclays, Berenberg, BMO, Canaccord, CIBC, Jefferies, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, National Bank, Raymond James, Scotiabank, Stifel, TD, UBS all Buy/Overweight/Outperform; RBC and Panmure Liberum more cautious at Sector Perform/Hold), with an average target price of GBP 49.22 versus a share price of GBP 47.42 as at 31 August 2026.

Guidance assumes $3,000/oz gold price and USD:EUR FX rate of 0.87; H1-2026 AISC of $1,871/oz (or $1,687/oz on a gold-price-adjusted basis net of $184/oz royalty impact from the higher realised price of $4,579/oz).
Raised from an initial $230m guidance; H1-2026 actual sustaining capex of $150m.
H1-2026 actual of $99m against the full-year target.
H1-2026 actual of $15m against the full-year target; expected to increase materially from 2027 if Assafou reaches FID.

items.target: at least $1.0bn (2026-2028), more than doubling potential if gold price is at/above $3,000/oz and leverage stays below 0.5x
items.notes: New Shareholder Returns Programme significantly increasing minimum returns versus the prior 2024-2025 $435m programme, while simultaneously funding Assafou construction; FY2025 actual returns were $435m (record).
Actual leverage at FY2025 year-end was 0.07x and net cash position of $254m at H1-2026, giving significant headroom versus the 0.5x target as Assafou capex ramps up.

items.target: 12-15Moz of Measured & Indicated mineral resources at <$40/oz discovery cost
items.vs_prior: new target (replaces prior 12-17Moz 2021-2025 target, which was achieved as 20.7Moz discovered since 2016)
items.notes: Split 6-9Moz brownfield and 6Moz greenfield, including up to three new tier-1 greenfield discoveries.
Represents ~27% growth versus FY2026 guidance midpoint, underpinned by Assafou and Sabodala-Massawa underground expansion; targets first-quartile AISC by 2030.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Ian Cockerill reiterated that the Group enters its next investment phase 'from a position of strength,' with FY2026 guidance 'on track' despite a seasonally weaker H1 weighted toward a stronger H2/Q4. Management emphasised that the balance sheet (0.07x-0.09x leverage through 2026) provides full flexibility to fund Assafou construction (FID targeted by year-end 2026) while simultaneously delivering a new, larger shareholder returns programme for 2026-2028. CFO Guy Young highlighted record H1-2026 free cash flow of $761m (+19% YoY) and noted the Group remains largely unhedged to continue capturing the benefit of the elevated gold price environment.

bull_case: Record gold price environment (sustained above $4,000/oz through mid-2026) combined with a largely unhedged production book provides substantial operating leverage, record free cash flow ($1.2bn in FY2025, record H1-2026 FCF of $761m) and funds both growth and shareholder returns simultaneously

Fortress balance sheet (0.07x net debt/EBITDA, net cash position, $1.2bn liquidity) gives Endeavour unusual flexibility among gold producers to fund the Assafou cornerstone project without re-leveraging or diluting shareholders, while still delivering an enhanced 2026-2028 shareholder returns programme of at least $1.0bn

Proven in-house project delivery track record (five consecutive builds on time and on budget, each in under two years) de-risks the execution of Assafou, which DFS economics show as a tier-1 asset (55% IRR, $5.1bn NPV at $4,000/oz gold)

Industry-leading exploration track record (20.7Moz discovered since 2016 at <$25/oz) with a credible new 12-15Moz/2026-2030 target supports long-term reserve replacement and production growth to 1.5Moz by 2030
Broad sell-side analyst support (consensus Buy/Outperform across ~16 of 18 covering brokers as of August 2026) with average target price modestly above the prevailing share price
bear_case: 100% single-commodity exposure to gold with essentially no hedging means earnings and valuation would compress sharply in a gold price correction from current historically elevated levels, and the company's own cost guidance and shareholder returns commitments are explicitly contingent on gold staying at/above $3,000/oz

Concentrated operations in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire and especially Burkina Faso expose the company to acute Sahel political/regulatory risk; the regional precedent of outright mine nationalisation (Burkina Faso's SOPAMIB takeover of the divested Boungou/Wahgnion mines, Mali's nationalisation of Yatela/Morila/SOMIFI) illustrates the tail risk inherent to West African gold mining even though Endeavour's current five-mine portfolio has not been directly targeted

Rising royalty costs at elevated gold prices are compressing AISC margins even as realised prices rise, with FY2026 AISC guidance ($1,600-1,800/oz) running well above FY2025 actual ($1,433/oz), partly offsetting the benefit of a higher gold price

Large, single-project growth concentration risk in Assafou - a delay to FID, cost overrun, or permitting/relocation issue at this complex cornerstone project would materially push back the 1.5Moz-by-2030 growth target that underpins the long-term investment case

Mining is inherently capital- and safety-intensive; a 2024 contractor fatality and a 2025 TRIFR increase above internal targets highlight ongoing operational risk, while reserve/resource depletion at maturing assets (e.g., Mana) requires continuous, successful (and not guaranteed) exploration investment
